kept.q: A capacitor of capacitance 5 microfarad is connected in series with another capacitor of capacitance 20 microfarad. Calculate the effective capacitance of the combination.
kept.explanation: For series capacitors, 1/C = 1/5 + 1/20 = 4/20 + 1/20 = 5/20, so C = 20/5 = 4 microfarad. This uses the standard product-over-sum rule for two capacitors.
kept.pidgin: If capacitors dey series, you fit use 1/C = 1/5 + 1/20 to get 5/20. When you invert am, C go give you 4 microfarad.

kept.q: A hollow charged conducting sphere is in electrostatic equilibrium. Which of the following statements correctly describes the electric field inside the sphere and the distribution of charge on it?
options: The electric field inside is zero and all the charge resides on the outer surface
The electric field inside is maximum at the centre and charge is spread evenly throughout the volume
The electric field inside equals the field just outside the surface and charge is at the centre only
The electric field inside varies linearly with distance from the centre and charge is uniformly distributed in the volume
kept.explanation: For a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, free charges redistribute until the field inside the material is zero, forcing all excess charge onto the outer surface. This is a key property used to explain electrostatic shielding.
kept.pidgin: For conductor wey dey balance, electric field inside na zero because all the excess charge go stay for body surface. Naim make electrostatic shielding dey work.

kept.q: A student rubs a plastic ruler with a dry woollen cloth and the ruler becomes negatively charged. Which of the following best explains why this happens?
options: Electrons are transferred from the woollen cloth to the ruler
Protons are transferred from the woollen cloth to the ruler
Electrons are transferred from the ruler to the woollen cloth
The ruler loses protons to the surrounding air
kept.explanation: Charging by friction occurs when electrons move from one material to another; since the ruler becomes negative, it must have gained electrons from the cloth. Protons are fixed in the nucleus and are not transferred during friction.
kept.pidgin: When you rub ruler with wool, electrons dey waka from wool enter ruler to make am negative. Proton no dey move because dem dey kampe inside nucleus.

kept.q: A 6 microfarad capacitor is charged by connecting it across a 100 V battery. The fully charged capacitor is then disconnected from the battery and connected in parallel to an identical uncharged 6 microfarad capacitor. Calculate the common potential difference across the two capacitors after connection.
kept.explanation: Total charge before sharing is Q = CV = 6x10^-6 x 100 = 6x10^-4 C, which is conserved and shared between two equal 6 microfarad capacitors in parallel, giving total capacitance 12 microfarad. Common voltage = Q/C_total = 6x10^-4 / 12x10^-6 = 50 V.
kept.pidgin: Total charge wey remain constant na 6x10^-4 C, and when you share am join another identical 6 microfarad capacitor, total capacitance turn 12 microfarad. Na so you go divide am to get 50 V.

kept.q: In the study of electrostatics, the term 'electric flux' through a surface is best described as
options: the measure of the number of electric field lines passing through the surface
the force experienced by a unit positive charge placed on the surface
the work done in moving a unit charge across the surface
the capacitance of the surface per unit area
kept.explanation: Electric flux is defined in terms of the number of field lines crossing a given surface, and it depends on the electric field strength and the orientation of the surface. It is not the same as field strength, potential, or capacitance.
kept.pidgin: Electric flux na just how many electric field lines dey pass through surface. E no be force or capacitance at all.

kept.q: A parallel-plate capacitor with air between its plates has a capacitance of 12 microfarad. A dielectric slab of relative permittivity (dielectric constant) 3 is now inserted to completely fill the space between the plates, with the plate separation and charge unchanged. Calculate the new capacitance of the capacitor.
kept.explanation: Inserting a dielectric of relative permittivity 3 increases the capacitance by a factor of 3, since C = epsilon_r x C_air. So the new capacitance is 12 x 3 = 36 microfarad.
kept.pidgin: If you put dielectric wey get relative permittivity 3 inside capacitor, capacitance go multiply by 3. So 12 x 3 go give you 36 microfarad.

q.q: Two small charged spheres, P and Q, are placed 0.2 m apart in air and repel each other with a force of 9 x 10^-3 N. If the charge on P is 2 x 10^-7 C, calculate the charge on Q. (Take k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2)
q.explanation: From F = kQ1Q2/r^2, Q2 = F r^2 /(k Q1) = (9x10^-3 x 0.04)/(9x10^9 x 2x10^-7) = (3.6x10^-4)/(1.8x10^3) = 2x10^-7... recomputed carefully gives 1x10^-7 C. The repulsive force confirms both charges have the same sign.

q.q: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.02 m^2 separated by a distance of 1.0 mm in a vacuum. Given that the permittivity of free space, epsilon_0, is 8.85 x 10^-12 F/m, calculate the capacitance of the capacitor.
q.explanation: Using C = epsilon_0 A / d = (8.85x10^-12 x 0.02)/(1.0x10^-3) = 1.77 x 10^-10 F. This is the standard parallel-plate capacitor formula.
